text: Installing fastembed (a small embedding model for meaning-based recall) was refused by the permission system on 2026-11-15; ask the person before trying again

2026-11-20: the person asked to compare He et al. 2024, 'Network model with internal complexity bridges AI and neuroscience' (Nat Comput Sci 4:584-599, doi 10.1038/s43588-024-00674-9, PMID 39152312; full text paywalled, read the abstract only) with the brain. Answer given: the brain is not a neural network; its tested parts are small fits (ridge logistic S1/P1-P3, least squares M1, sigma-scaled range W1). Richer learners were already tried and failed on unseen data (P9 attention head, P10 market model, the REM residual network). The paper's 'rich unit' idea fits only the size side, where the brain has skill: a possible W2 (a per-stock unit with its own memory of calm and storm in place of W1's sigma) was offered as a new declared test, not built.

2026-11-20: the person clarified: compare the paper (He et al. 2024, HH vs LIF, internal complexity) with our neuron model, not the market. Our model is brain/neurons on branch claude/sleepy-goldberg-2ma18z (not on upbeat-turing): Izhikevich cells (2 variables, between LIF's 1 and HH's 4), conductance synapses with reversal potentials and per-synapse delays, hand-wired by rules, 11-simplex cliques, Pong 107 / Runner 77 / Catch about 1,350 neurons, one plastic layer plus trust-earned learning from peers. Offered: add HH and LIF cells to the simulator and measure how many neurons each needs for the same Catch score, and noise robustness (Catch 75% fell to 32% at noise 2).

2026-11-23: Kymera started a proposed $1.5bn share sale after the close, the same day the mosaic gave it 7.4% (usual 0.9%) for a share sale in 20 sessions. Check flaws found that day, not yet fixed: the case file prints 2-in-3 numbers under the 9-in-10 label; attention treats a call judged on asof as open (AMD); the case file's cash line leaves out investments (Capricor had about $198.5m with investments, not $44.3m); after-close market/driver lines compare with the previous close (false market-wide flag).
